text:
lia: After the RBAC canary rollout were seeing an uptick in SCIM 403s tied to assertion decrypt. ~15% of creates failing. sample log below.

marc: paste? which tenants/IdPs?

lia: Mostly EU tenants on Okta and a couple Azure AD. sample: 
```
scim-provisioner ERROR user=svc_alex@example.com err="kms:decrypt: unsupported_encryption_profile" details="jwe.header={"alg":"A256GCM","enc":"A256GCM"}"
http 403 {"error":"decrypt_failed","key_arn":"arn:aws:kms:eu-west-1:123:key/tenant123"}
```

oncall-bot: incident created: https://incidents.redwood/INC-2026-scim-decrypt-spike priority=P2

kms-bot: key/tenant123 last-rotate=3724998000 supported_algorithms=["RSA-OAEP","RSA-OAEP-256"]

marc: Looks like IdP switched attribute encryption to a JWE/AES-GCM profile (direct CEK) vs our expected RSA-wrapped CEK. We don't have the symmetric key so KMS cannot decrypt.

security: immediate actions: pause RBAC canary writes that trigger provisioning, enable masked logging (no raw assertions), and enqueue failed SCIM ops to backfill queue. Notify CS to contact tenants.

lia: paused canary and flipped masked logging flag. failures queued to backfill-s3. CS notified and Okta ticket opened.

marc: medium-term: update envelope parser to detect alg!=RSA-OAEP and return clear error strings (jwe-direct-unsupported), add metric scim.decrypt.fail_reason, and update runbook with tenant outreach template.

security: long-term options: tenant changes to RSA-OAEP (preferred) OR implement a customer-managed-key integration where tenant KMS supplies wrapped CEKs we can unwrap, but that requires legal changes and policy reviews. Add unit tests for alg detection and masked logging.

lia: thanks everyone. keeping thread for incident notes & postmortem. :thumbsup:
